content: Indication-specific dosing for aloe includes the following regimens: oral administration of 50-200 mg per day, 30 ml orally three times daily, or 15-60 drops orally as needed. For topical use, a 1:10 dilution with 50% alcohol can be applied 3-5 times daily as needed. Aloe is used to promote wound healing and is also utilized for its anesthetic, antiseptic, and anti-inflammatory properties. It is commonly applied for conditions such as arthritis, burns, cold sores, fever, inflammation, pruritis, and as a moisturizer. Aloe is possibly effective for alleviating pain, reducing inflammation, and promoting wound healing. It may also have hypoglycemic effects, although no significant adverse effects have been reported in this regard. However, oral use of aloe may cause abdominal discomfort and is contraindicated in conditions such as appendicitis, Crohn's disease, diabetes mellitus, hemorrhoids, intestinal obstruction, kidney disease, nausea/vomiting, peptic ulcer disease (PUD), and ulcerative colitis. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, aloe is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. However, specific pregnancy and lactation categories are not available (N/A).
